claims.statement: URE explains that distribution tariffs contain charges for excess reactive power and contracted-capacity exceedance, and that reactive-power compensation, contract-power changes or tariff changes can reduce specific bill items.
URE specifically recommends analyzing distribution invoices and consumption profiles before cost-saving action.
A verified-savings contract may be easier to buy than a generic energy audit because payment follows a measurable reduction.
The distribution of recoverable annual savings among reachable Polish SMEs under current 2026 tariffs is unknown.

contrary_evidence: Electricians, energy brokers and compensation-equipment vendors already offer audits, sometimes free to sell hardware.
The cited URE explanation establishes charge mechanics but not current tariff amounts or the size of the addressable leakage.
Some sites need capital equipment with long payback, and savings can be confounded by production changes.

economics.acquisition_route: Acquire customers through accountants, energy brokers, electricians, photovoltaic installers and the founder's family business; begin with a no-saving, no-fee invoice audit.
economics.founder_time: Part-time validation hypothesis; delivery burden remains untested.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A cross-DSO dataset of invoice formats, facility load signatures, interventions, equipment cost and realized savings can improve eligibility scoring and avoid uneconomic site visits.
fingerprint.customer: Polish SMEs and multi-site operators on non-household electricity tariffs, particularly facilities with motors, refrigeration, LED lighting, UPS systems, photovoltaic installations or recent electrical modifications.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Acquire customers through accountants, energy brokers, electricians, photovoltaic installers and the founder's family business; begin with a no-saving, no-fee invoice audit.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Invoice and interval-data ingestion that identifies charge components, simulates tariff and capacity choices, flags reactive-power patterns, routes a scoped measurement visit and verifies savings after compensation equipment or contract changes.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The facility pays the distribution bill every month. Charge a contingency share of independently verified savings for the first year, plus an optional monitoring subscription; hardware and electrician work remain separately quoted.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A monthly distribution invoice starts or continues charging for excess reactive power, excess contracted capacity or a poorly matched tariff, often after load or equipment changes that finance staff cannot interpret.

founder_fit: Excellent match for quantitative modeling and family access to electrical customers.
Success-fee validation controls customer and founder downside.
Can start as analysis software with partner-delivered hardware installation.
risks: Evidence of a workflow, transition, or loss does not yet establish recurring willingness to pay.
The proposed distribution and compounding mechanisms remain hypotheses pending buyer evidence.

title: Reactive-power and contracted-capacity leakage auditor
uncertainties: Share of audited SMEs with enough avoidable charges to support acquisition and electrician costs.
Availability and permissioning of interval meter data across DSOs.
A measurement and verification method robust to weather, occupancy and production changes.
Pricing, buyer authority, and acquisition economics remain unvalidated at discovery.

First validation test: Audit 100 recent invoices from at least 30 unrelated firms reached through accountants and installers, then meter the 10 strongest sites before any intervention. Request signed contingency agreements only where a conservative payback is under 12 months and verify savings against a pre-agreed baseline for three billing cycles.
